name: mycrew
description: A five-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer driving the one below: primitives and house rules, a pipeline that carries a task from decision to hardened code, a product plane holding what the product must do, a board holding what is being done about it right now, and the crew that builds it — a chief over the whole product, a lead to a feature, a worker to an assignment. Beside the layers stand the specialists, a plugin each and only where the trade is substantial enough to earn one: agent-warden is the first, watching the sessions and stopping what wandered. Install mycrew-tools first.

plugins.name: mycrew-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/5 — the primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you reach for mid-work: /slap resets a fix that has stopped working, /likec4 draws architecture as code, /reminder pins a rule as a hard constraint, /retract hunts down information declared wrong and cuts it out. Ships the house rule files too. Everything above builds on this.

plugins.name: mycrew-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/5 — the build pipeline. Six stages carry one task from a decision to shipped code: /how-to-do settles the fork, /do builds it, then /refactor, /review, /secure and /test harden it. In review and secure, the eyes that hunt are never the author's. Every stage weighs what actually changed and skips in one honest line when the change doesn't earn it.

plugins.name: mycrew-product
plugins.description: Layer 3/5 — the product plane: everything true about the whole product, above the sub-projects. /product-init founds it. /braindump and /ask-me draw the product out of you and file each piece where it belongs; /propose-idea is the one that puts an idea in, and only on your approval. Whatever you affirm, wherever you affirm it, product-rules is the one rule set that decides where it lands and in what shape.

plugins.name: mycrew-board
plugins.description: Layer 4/5 — the board: what is being done right now about what the plane says the product must be. Built on backlog.md, so tasks are plain markdown in the repo and the same board opens in a terminal or a browser. Every task carries where it came from — asked for by the human, or thought up by an agent and waiting to be approved — the feature it serves, and criteria somebody other than its executor can check. /board-init stands it up over the features the plane already holds; board-rules governs what a task carries and who may move it.

plugins.name: mycrew-crew
plugins.description: Layer 5/5 — the crew: the ones who actually build the product. Three characters, each handing down to the next. The chief is your deputy over the whole product, one to a product, owning the plane and delegating each approved feature whole. A lead holds one feature across every repo it touches, spawned as a background session of its own and reaching the other leads only where its feature depends on theirs. A worker carries one assignment end to end through the pipeline and hands back a four-field report. Each carries how it runs the rung below, so there is nothing to load and nothing to forget. Only the worker writes code.

plugins.name: agent-warden
plugins.description: A specialist, not a layer — the watch that stands over everything the layers do. Start a session as @warden and it sees every other session in the project: at each trigger it asks whether the work still serves what you asked for, takes your own corrections as standing rules, stops what wandered and puts it through /why-do-it, and comes to you only with what the gate could not settle. /warden-stop and /warden-start put the watch down and pick it up without losing the session. Every trigger leaves a line on disk, so the whole watch reads back afterwards. It judges and stops; it never does the work and never says how.
